newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia crime levels below U.S., Europe -ministry.
newsitem.headline: Russia crime levels below U.S., Europe -ministry.

text.p: An interior ministry official, defending Moscow's crime-fighting record, said on Tuesday registered crime levels in Russia were below those in the United States and most countries of western Europe.
"The crime rate in Russia is inside global limits," Igor Zubov, deputy head of the interior ministry's general staff, told Interfax news agency.

He said registered criminal cases amounted to 1,800 per 100,000 Russians. Comparative figures per 100,000 people were 15,000 criminal cases in the United States, 14,000 in Sweden and 8,300 in Germany.

But registered crime does not fully reflect the criminal situation in Russia, where people are often scared to report extortion of money or even car thefts, preferring to seek "protection" from criminal groups.
Interior Ministry officials have also acknowledged that local police stations are sometimes reluctant to register crimes which they think could reflect badly on them.
Five years of transition to a market economy have channelled vast resources into private hands and generated a wave of organised crime.
Mafia-style gangs across Russia are involved in extortion and contract killings of businessmen, bankers and officials, as well as robberies, money laundering and drug trafficking.
